finding: ARBS's shell k=2 ('Spectral / Analytical') lists 'L, Spec(L), H(t), delta_spec' as its Object contents -- but this is just the NEXT node in the 8-stage pipeline, populated by whatever graph occupies shell k=1's 'G' node. ARBS itself defines no 'hypergraph Laplacian' or native spectral operator ACTING ON ITS OWN Object/Operator/hyperedge structure -- shell k=2 simply says 'once you have a G, take its ordinary Laplacian L=D-A and decompose it,' which is BRIDGE B-001 (G->L, CERTIFIED) and BRIDGE B-002 (L->Spec(L), CERTIFIED) -- both stated for an ARBITRARY graph G=(V,E,W), not specifically for a graph derived from ARBS's own hypergraph structure.
Spec(L_ARBS)_defined: NO. There is no 'L_ARBS' object anywhere in source distinct from 'whatever L=D-A arises from whatever G was chosen.' The question 'is Spec(L_ARBS)=Spec(L(G_k))' therefore has no well-formed left-hand side to compare against.
consequence: Spec(L(G_k)) -- the spectrum I have computed, verified, and used throughout runs 1-9 -- is a completely legitimate, CORRECTLY COMPUTED spectrum of the EXPLICIT graph G_k. Bridges B-001 (G->L) and B-002 (L->Spec(L)) are CERTIFIED and apply to it exactly as they would to any graph. What is NOT established is that G_k is THE G that ARBS's shell k=1 refers to (see arbs_graph_projection.json, CASE D) -- so while the MECHANICS (G->L->Spec(L)) are certified and correctly applied, the SPECIFIC INPUT (G_k) has not been shown to be an ARBS-sanctioned choice.
